issues: Abstract drift risk is elevated: intake does not sufficiently lock object-first behavior.
fixes: Add anti-drift rules and explicit bans on texture-only, atmosphere-first, and abstract-first outcomes.

revised_intake.creative_intent: Conduct an extreme macro material study of a single manufactured object, the Mikage Zenith Blade, specifically focusing on achieving a clean matte B4C technical ceramic read for its primary body, while preserving the blade's engineered form and sharp edge geometry.

must_have: readable contour evidence of a greatsword blade
exactly one manufactured object as the clear subject
visible contour evidence such as edge, rim, bevel, seam, or curvature
material visibly attached to the object, not floating as texture
visible edge, rim, bevel, seam, or contour evidence
material visibly attached to the object

composition.framing: Close-up on a single manufactured object, fully readable as one object
composition.camera: Detailed, sharp focus on material and form

constraints: Emphasize material texture and finish without glare

core_risks: Drifting into abstract forms or texture-only images
Losing the manufactured object's identity or contour
Material reads resembling forbidden finishes (e.g., glossy plastic, plaster)
Contamination by unwanted colors or atmospheric effects
material misread as plaster, stone, or glossy plastic
anti_drift_rules: Lock the object read to a single, identifiable manufactured object (Mikage Zenith Blade)
Prevent abstract drift by maintaining clear object contours and structure
Suppress any texture-only, atmosphere-first, or subject-loss outcomes
Ensure the material read is explicitly B4C technical ceramic and not any forbidden material
always preserve one clearly readable manufactured object
do not let texture or atmosphere become the subject
keep material identity locked and explicit
do not allow abstract, texture-only, or atmosphere-first subject drift
keep material identity explicit and stable
success_criteria: Immediate readability of the Mikage Zenith Blade as a straight, engineered greatsword
Clean, unambiguous matte B4C technical ceramic material read for the primary body
Dry, dense, engineered finish is clearly evident
Absence of all forbidden material reads and finishes
Sharp edge readability and industrial construction are preserved
image does not collapse into abstract texture or atmosphere
image does not read as plaster, stone, or glossy plastic
revised_intake.direction_summary: Focus on an extreme macro study of the Mikage Zenith Blade, prioritizing a clean, matte B4C technical ceramic material read for its main body. Maintain the object's clear, engineered form and sharp edges against a dark, minimal background with controlled low-key lighting. Strictly avoid any abstract drift, texture-only outcomes, or forbidden material reads.
